dimensions.explanation: The control concerns submission events to IPD for investment products it administers. The text does not restrict the obligation to a named class of banks, licensees or individual users. Reporting requests are included; annual-fee settlement is described separately.

The footnote lists relevant product categories; the background identifies new applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions. WINGS is expanded, but detailed boundaries of a submission event and IPD administration are not supplied.

Existing channels remain accepted during the extended parallel run. No post-cutover exemption, outage dispensation or grandfathering provision is stated. Optional annual-fee payment is a separate capability, rather than an exception to mandatory submission.
'Must' establishes the submission-route requirement. 'Will be integrated' describes system integration; 'can also settle' permits annual-fee payment without requiring that payment route.

The extended parallel run ends on 29 November 2024 and mandatory use begins on 30 November 2024. The original 29 October end date is superseded. Treatment of follow-up acts on existing cases is not expressly detailed.

The 8 July 2024 circular is referenced but not supplied. Dependency missing.4ad6b317ad4ade41b82f120a has no supplied text or hash; its identity and effect cannot be established. Neither omission supplies evidence of an exception.

questions: Does the referenced 8 July 2024 circular or the missing dependency specify treatment of follow-up submissions for cases opened before the cutover?
What event fixes the submission date where transmission, receipt and acceptance fall on different dates?
Does any supplied-later authoritative material define exclusions or outage arrangements? None is stated in this packet.

assumptions: The selected control evaluates one application or submission event, not the compliance of an institution as a whole.
A submission event is classified using its substance and IPD administration; the fact supplier must resolve uncertain classifications.
The event date is supplied as a Gregorian date. The packet does not resolve transmission-versus-receipt timing.
Extension of the parallel run preserves the described acceptance of existing channels through 29 November 2024.
No grandfathering rule is inferred merely because a case began before the cutover.

citations.quote: After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
new product applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions to IPD.
During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing.
In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.

1 Investment-linked assurance schemes, mandatory provident fund products, open-ended fund companies, paper gold schemes, pooled retirement funds, real estate investment trusts, unit trusts and mutual funds and unlisted structured investment products.

readings.distinction: The strongest supported reading attaches the cutover to each submission event. For example, an IPD-administered fund's NAV report submitted on 30 November 2024 through the old system fails this selected route control, even if the fund was authorised earlier. A fee-only payment outside e-IP does not fail this control merely because of its route. The packet supports neither a general grandfathering alternative nor mandatory e-IP payment of annual fees; treating either as a competing rule would invent ambiguity. The strongest uncertainty concerns follow-up acts in pending cases and the event fixing their submission date.
